notes: Botanical extract sometimes used for lipid and bile-flow support. Meta-analyses of randomized trials suggest modest

  - stress/anxiety/sleep positioning is plausible for review, while thyroid, liver, sedative, BP/glucose-medication, and serotonergic

notes: Low-dose 81 mg enteric-coated aspirin / acetylsalicylic acid drug-like product. Enteric coating delays action and is
  not for fast headache relief. Antiplatelet bleeding-risk stacking should be reviewed with omega-3, nattokinase, and similar

notes: 'Carotenoid antioxidant from Haematococcus pluvialis microalgae (or krill). Soft food preference is bounded and formulation/lipid-sensitive; evidence is insufficient to establish fat_meal_required. Typical dose 4–12 mg/day. Human/formulation sources: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19734684/ and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12885395/.'

notes: BaCognize Ultra branded bacopa extract used in Life Extension Adrenal Energy Formula proprietary blend; per-component
  amount not disclosed by label. Established acetylcholinesterase inhibitor (StatPearls NBK589635) — contributes to cholinergic

notes: Beetroot extract or juice concentrate is usually modeled for dietary nitrate, nitrate to nitrite to nitric-oxide biology,
  vascular tone, and exercise economy or endurance context. Evidence is stronger for nitrate-rich beetroot juice and standardized
  nitrate dosing than for unspecified beetroot powders or extracts, so label nitrate amount matters. Source refs include PMID
  23580439, PMID 24791915, and PMID 41515267.

notes: Plant alkaloid commonly proposed for cardiometabolic support. Meta-analyses report lipid and glucose-marker improvements
  in some populations, but study quality, heterogeneity, product form, and medication-interaction context make this a review
  candidate rather than a routine LDL-C recommendation.

notes: Pre-workout amino acid in this stack context. Added as a known substance for future relation modeling around glycine,
  beta-alanine, and taurine receptor competition. Review context - carnosine/buffering and paresthesia/tolerance are dose-dependent
  and not computed by the planner.

notes: Marker polysaccharide component listed on Real Mushrooms Lion's Mane as beta-(1,3)(1,6)-glucans. Kept as a substance

notes: Knowledge-only leucine-metabolite sports-nutrition reference card. Added because HMB is a common muscle-preservation

notes: Knowledge-only gastric-acidifier reference card. Added because betaine HCl is a common digestive-support supplement

notes: Anthocyanin-rich berry extract with vascular and ocular-health positioning. Mild antiplatelet potential at concentrated

notes: Knowledge-only menopause-support botanical reference card. Added because black cohosh is one of the best-known nonhormonal
  menopause supplement categories, but evidence for menopause symptoms is inconsistent and liver-safety/product-identity review

notes: Generic elemental boron contribution. The active Life Extension product supplies 3 mg from a citrate/aspartate/glycinate complex; calcium fructoborate is a distinct inactive source and its evidence does not transfer to generic boron. NIH ODS does not classify boron as an essential human nutrient and does not establish a clear human function. Limited and inconsistent human evidence concerns bone/mineral, hormone, cognition, vitamin-D/calcium, and metabolic outcomes; no form has an established advantage. Keep intake within bounded upper-intake context; no known clinical medication interaction is established.

notes: Anti-inflammatory gum extract; mild antiplatelet potential and CYP modulation reported. Joint-comfort evidence is suggestive

notes: Caffeine anhydrous stimulant form listed on ALLMAX Essentials Caffeine 200 mg tablets.

notes: Choline component listed on Jarrow MaculaPF as coming from sunflower lecithin. Product cards keep source-specific labels

notes: >-
  Choline bitartrate form disclosed on the GLS Ежовик гребенчатый с холином label;
  the physical label amount is 160 mg choline bitartrate per capsule and is not
  reinterpreted as elemental choline. Choline is an essential nutrient with
  intrinsic roles in acetylcholine synthesis, methyl-group metabolism, and
  phospholipid membrane structure; these physiological roles do not establish
  cognitive enhancement. Human TMAO formation is dependent on choline form,
  exposure, and gut-microbiome context; biomarker findings do not establish
  clinical harm, a clinical risk threshold, or a schedule. The planner is
  dose-agnostic.

notes: Sulfated glycosaminoglycan / cartilage substrate. A and C isomers are encoded as one card because they differ only
  in sulfation position and share scheduling behavior. Used in Animal Flex Joint Construction Complex.

notes: Generic elemental chromium contribution. Product cards keep the concrete source form in component labels and notes.
  This card represents supplemental trivalent chromium (Cr(III)), not toxic industrial hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)); concrete
  source forms remain on product cards. FNB 2001 treated chromium as essential, whereas EFSA 2014 did not substantiate
  essentiality or set dietary reference values. The mineral kind classification is elemental, not an essentiality claim.
  NIH ODS describes chromium in an insulin-action / glucose-metabolism context, but routine glycemic benefit is mixed and any
  body-composition effect is trivial. EFSA 2008 is used here for source safety, not efficacy or scheduling.

notes: 'Histamine H2-receptor antagonist. Gastric acid inhibitors can reduce absorption of food-bound vitamin B12. Source:

notes: Ubiquinone form listed on California Gold Nutrition Nicotinamide Riboside Tartrate Complex; electron-transport-chain

notes: Chelated copper form used where labels call out bisglycinate/glycinate chelate. Copper is a cuproenzyme cofactor for
  energy production, iron metabolism, connective tissue synthesis, neurotransmitter synthesis, and copper-containing superoxide
  dismutases. NIH ODS notes that sustained high zinc intake can impair copper absorption and gives an adult UL of 10 mg/day;
  EFSA 10.2903/j.efsa.2008.718 is a general copper source, not evidence that bisglycinate is superior to other forms. No general
  meal, clock-time, or activity schedule is established.

notes: Inorganic copper salt used in Optimum Nutrition Opti-Men. Kept separate from chelated copper forms because source form
  is a practical tolerance/review distinction; copper dose and zinc balance need manual review per NIH ODS.

notes: Mycelial cordyceps extract used in Life Extension Adrenal Energy Formula proprietary blend; per-component amount not
  disclosed by label. Adaptogen with energy and endurance positioning; mild HR/BP/immunomodulatory effects possible, relevant
  in vascular-review context.

notes: Berry source of proanthocyanidins; commonly used for urinary-tract and antioxidant context. Polyphenol load may carry
  mild antiplatelet potential at concentrated extract doses.

notes: 'Concrete fish-oil concentrate identity for the Solgar Omega-3 product. The
  official formulation supplies 1400 mg fish-oil concentrate per softgel and 950 mg

  krill oil. Bleeding is a conditional medication and surgery review context, not a

notes: 'Omega-3 oil from Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba). notes: Amino acid and nitric-oxide pathway precursor. Added as a known substance for future relation modeling around lysine

notes: 'Acetylated form of L-carnitine; crosses the blood-brain barrier unlike plain L-carnitine. Dual action: mitochondrial
  support (shuttles acetyl groups into the TCA cycle) and cholinergic modulation (donates acetyl group for ACh synthesis).
  Typical dose 500–2000 mg/day; current evidence does not support a universal morning, empty-stomach, or bedtime-avoidance
  scheduling rule. TMAO production via gut microbiome warrants caution
  in cardiovascular risk profiles. Sources: examine.com (Acetyl-L-Carnitine), Malaguarnera et al. 2007 (Am J Clin Nutr).'

notes: 'L-tartrate salt form of L-carnitine. LCLT supports peripheral mitochondrial fatty-acid transport context; recovery and TMAO implications remain bounded, host-context-dependent review topics. Sources: NIH ODS Carnitine; DailyMed levocarnitine; PMID 15591001; PMID 17313301; PMID 34684429; PMID 34959912; PMID 23563705; Primecraft label.'
notes: 'Active unbranded 5 g has an unresolved citrulline:malate ratio; human evidence supports arginine/NO-cGMP biology but vascular/exercise outcomes are mixed.'
